scope: Local synthetic signed-transaction, private temporary filesystem and RPC fixtures only; one compatibility case uses actual loopback HTTP. No new Agave journal handoff, validator start, signing service, production endpoint or broadcast.
checks: Version2 preparation binds source/destination identities, side, mint, exact ELF/full ProgrammeData/upgrade-authority/static-policy pins to signed claim
Both handoff entries enforce committed pins for version2; pinned-only entry refuses legacy records; historical version1 remains compatible
Two finalized snapshots per side before and after fresh source-event observation, same epoch/precision/full5-key committee and unpaused settlement
Late code/authority/policy change, expiry or regressing height, new consumed receipt, wrong genesis, stale context and outage refuse handoff with identical prepared journal bytes
Native release and original-token redemption hand out exact original signed bytes once; exclusive lock prevents concurrent duplicate handoff
Later same-signature reconciliation advances checkpoint and remains inspectable; pre-handoff expiry has no fabricated admission and cannot enable retry
Input mutation and corrupt committed policy/admission reject; no sendTransaction or fresh blockhash requests
coverageLimits: Programme snapshots do not prove historical source execution under the same code or prevent authorized upgrade after the final read
Policy hash is a digest, not authentication against a local journal writer or signer custody compromise
Legacy schema1 keeps original unpinned rehearsal semantics and cannot gain retrospective acceptance
No new ledger copies, keys on remote worker, nonces or bridge transactions; all retained private branches preserved
Fresh private-ledger integration, production custody/upgrade controls, independent history/backing/finality and external security review remain open
